sections.strategy: Next's first-half 2026 results (reported 17 September, still driving City commentary into this week) showed pre-tax profit up 10.5% to £569m and full-price sales up 7.7% to 1 August, with full-year profit guidance nudged up £12m to £1.255bn — the fourth upgrade this year. Management credited hot weather and international growth for offsetting continued softness in UK store sales; no new brand, TOTAL Platform partner, or acquisition news surfaced this week.
sections.pricing: Shares traded in a 14,000–14,780p range through the week, dipping below the 50-day moving average around 20 September before recovering to c.14,575p by 25 September (+1.2% on the day) on continued digestion of the H1 upgrade. Analyst consensus held at Hold (3 Buy, 5 Hold) with an average price target of £153.55 (range £140–187); Citigroup reiterated a neutral stance, and the stock remains below most price targets.
soWhat: A fourth guidance upgrade this year signals resilient full-price sell-through despite UK softness — suppliers should expect steady-to-growing replenishment volumes rather than order cutbacks heading into autumn/winter.
City sentiment is cautious (Hold consensus, price targets clustered near or below the current share price) — no signal yet of an aggressive expansion or supply-base build-out driven by the upgrade.

No supplier list, sustainability, sourcing, or TOTAL Platform announcements this week means no new compliance, certification, or onboarding requirements for Tier 1 vendors — an operationally quiet week worth noting as 'no change' rather than a monitoring gap.
